policy: Textbook photos are private and authoritative for drawing-oriented subdivision. Web sources are secondary anatomical cross-checks. Public repo stores metadata/rules only, never the private images.

textbook_rules: Difficult-angle foot may be decomposed into ankle, foot body, hallux, toes 2-5, and sole/heel landmarks.
Sole reference uses hallux, four-toe group, medial ball, lateral ball and heel as stable landmarks.
Heel/Achilles, toe direction and ankle geometry must remain coherent from front, side and rear views.

web_sources.title: Kenhub - Sole of foot
web_sources.lesson: The plantar surface is distinct from the dorsum; ball of foot lies beneath metatarsal heads and heel beneath calcaneus.

textbook_rules: Use local shoulder-to-elbow-to-wrist progression instead of whole-body height to divide the arm.
Drawing simplification may group the anterior and posterior forearm while retaining biceps/triceps and elbow/wrist transitions.
Axillary lines are relationships among deltoid, pectoralis, biceps/triceps and latissimus rather than horizontal rings.

web_sources.title: Kenhub - Superficial anterior forearm muscles
web_sources.lesson: Anterior forearm contains superficial flexor/pronator muscles sharing proximal relationships around the medial epicondyle.

web_sources.title: Kenhub - Superficial posterior forearm muscles
web_sources.lesson: Posterior forearm contains the superficial extensor group; brachioradialis is superficial on the radial side.

web_sources.title: Kenhub - Brachioradialis
web_sources.lesson: Brachioradialis forms a visible lateral boundary between anterior and posterior forearm compartments.

textbook_rules: Finger drawing structure is proximal, middle and distal segments; thumb is treated separately.
Hand/finger segmentation must not be inferred only from global body height.

web_sources.title: Wikimedia Commons - Phalanges of the hand, dorsal view
web_sources.lesson: Open reference for phalange location and dorsal orientation; source data from BodyParts3D.

web_sources.title: Wikimedia Commons - Phalanges of the hand, palmar view
web_sources.lesson: Open reference for phalange location and palmar orientation.

textbook_rules: Deltoid overlaps/bridges shoulder and upper arm; its silhouette and boundary change with arm elevation.
Axillary hollow is a triangular relationship among pectoralis major, latissimus, deltoid and upper-arm structures.
Raised-arm views must be checked from front, rear and side; a static horizontal boundary is insufficient.

web_sources.title: Kenhub - Fascias and spaces of the shoulder girdle
web_sources.lesson: Axillary fascia spans relationships between pectoral and latissimus regions and contributes to the axillary hollow.

textbook_rules: Back review must distinguish central trapezius/scapular context from lateral latissimus and thoracolumbar context.
Shoulder movement changes the visible relation between deltoid, rotator cuff/scapular region and latissimus.
